## Objective

Make `run` in `kernel.py` faster than AKLR's baseline on as many of the 25 workloads below as
possible, keeping every one of them correct: a candidate that wins on time and loses a workload is rejected.

## Contract

- `fused_moe`: Route each token to its top-k experts, run both projections, combine.
- Attributes: `{"activation": "swiglu", "quant_type": "per_1x32", "doweight_stage1": false, "gate_mode": "separated", "has_expert_mask": false, "has_swiglu_limit": true, "act_quant": 4}`. Inputs: `hidden_states`, `w1`, `w2`, `topk_weights`, `topk_ids`, `w1_scale`, `w2_scale`, `swiglu_limit`. Outputs: `out`.
- Fixed axes: `model_dim=6144, n_experts=128, topk=4, inter_dim=768, gate_up_rows=1536, model_blocks=192, inter_blocks=24`. Varying axes: `n_tokens`.
- `run` takes AKLR's call keys as keyword arguments and writes each output into its preallocated argument;
  it returns nothing and allocates no output.
- `kernel.py` may import modules beside it relatively (`from .helpers import f`): those modules are part of the
  kernel AKLR publishes; a file `kernel.py` does not reach, such as a probe, is not.
- AKLR compares the outputs with `{"max_violation_fraction": 0.001, "determinism": "bounded", "element_order": "fixed"}`.
- Every shape, dtype, layout and error bound is in the schema: `/home/ruibzhan/aklr-moe-m31-20261105/run-large/schema.json`.

# AKLR kernel knowledge base

What makes a kernel fast on AMD GPUs inside AKLR, by op and by symptom. The `flydsl_` cards and the cases come
from FlyDSL kernels: their mechanisms carry to other languages, their numbers were measured on FlyDSL code (re-derive
them: § Rules that hold everywhere), and their code is FlyDSL. How to write it in
a language is in that language's folder: `flydsl/SKILL.md`, `triton/SKILL.md`, `hip/SKILL.md`.

Paths below are relative to this folder, except those starting with `aklr/`, relative to the repository root, and
`aiter/` or `csrc/`, relative to aiter's. File and line citations are to ROCm/FlyDSL `v0.3.2` (`dd8373349`),
AMD-AGI/Primus-Turbo main `7615a5a2` (`ca1fdd67` for the expert GEMM in `moe/`) and ROCm/aiter `dbd8bf5`
(`AKLR_BASELINE_AITER`); check out those revisions to follow them. FlyDSL's own skills are linked at `v0.3.2`, not
copied: `flydsl/guides.md` and `profile.md` give each link with what this repository corrects in it; a
`§` marked as FlyDSL's is that skill's own numbering.

## Stop: what a AKLR kernel cannot do

`aklr/ops/README.md` § The kernel section and ABI is the authority; where this skill disagrees, the README
wins. Check a plan against this table before writing code.

| Rule | What it rules out here |
|---|---|
| Outputs pass the definition's `compare` block; under `determinism: bitwise`, the default, two runs are byte-identical (`runs_agree`, `aklr/core/contract/semantics/_compare.py`) | Reducing in arrival order (atomic split-K, stream-K fix-ups): reduce in a fixed order (`gemm/flydsl_gemm_correctness.md` §8, `gemm/flydsl_gemm_grid_pricing.md` §2) |
| A Point is served by the file with the best measured `speedup` over the baseline, and only from `AKLR_MIN_SPEEDUP` (1.03) | Judging on a mean: compare each Point with the faster of the kernel AKLR serves there and the baseline |
| Launch code (`run` and what it calls) does not synchronize, call `.item()` / `.cpu()`, print, read a clock or the environment, or change torch state (SA3) | Timing or racing configurations in `run` |
| Compilation and the choice of configuration happen in a module-level `@functools.cache` function on a Point's first call; later calls may be inside a CUDA graph capture | The first-call race of `gemm/flydsl_gemm_autotune.md` §1 as written: choose from the shape, with a table raced offline |
| Inputs other than the mutable ones are read-only (SA2); nothing derived from an argument is kept across calls, and there is no `global` or `nonlocal` (SA1) | Caching a repacked weight: repack on every call, or serve the contract's shuffled layout variant where it has one |
| Scratch is allocated in the call (`torch.empty`: contents undefined) or once per shape in the compile function and rewritten before it is read; no call depends on what an earlier call left | Counters that live across calls: zero workspaces in each call before any read (`gemm/flydsl_gemm_small_m.md` §4) |
| No workgroup waits for another: nothing polls a flag or data that another workgroup of the launch writes, since a launch's workgroups need not all be resident (a stream limited to part of the CUs, another kernel holding CUs) | A split-K fold or split-KV merge whose owner polls its partners: merge in a separate launch, or have each publish and count in on an atomic counter and the last to arrive merge, in a fixed order |
| `run(*, <kernel_call_keys>)` writes the preallocated outputs and returns nothing; the entry file's docstring describes the kernel, with no history or speedup (SA4) | Allocating outputs; importing sibling files other than relatively (the package name is a hash) |

## How to look things up

- Before opening a page, write down the diagnosis so far (the regime and the trace or counter that shows it),
  the plan, and the one question whose answer would change the plan.
- Pick one page and one section with the tables below, and read that, not the folder.
- Then note what changed in the plan, and leave one line in the round's notes: `KB: matched <page> §<n>` or
  `KB: no-match <question>`. The no-match lines are what this skill is missing.
- Confirm a change by what its page says to check (final ISA, kernel descriptor, a counter), not by the total
  time alone.
- Before starting on an op, look in [cases/INDEX.md](cases/INDEX.md) for a delivered kernel of the same op and
  regime, and in [pitfalls/INDEX.md](pitfalls/INDEX.md) for its traps.

## By task

| Task | Read in this order |

| Write or optimize a dense GEMM (fp8 / MXFP4 / MXFP8 / bf16) | `gemm/INDEX.md` → the card it routes to |
| A GEMM with M ≤ 256 (decode, speculative verify) | `gemm/flydsl_gemm_small_m.md` |

| A MoE: fused MoE at decode sizes (MXFP4, routing sort, stage 1 / stage 2), or its expert grouped GEMM (forward, dgrad, variable-K wgrad) | `moe/INDEX.md` → the card it routes to; the expert GEMM is its § Expert GEMM (grouped GEMM), with main loop and datapath in `gemm/` |
| Write or optimize an attention kernel (prefill, backward, decode with split KV) | `attention/INDEX.md` → the card it routes to |
| Dump a kernel's IR and final ISA; read registers, LDS, spills, waits and hot-loop counts | `gemm/flydsl_gemm_mainloop.md` §10 (`FLYDSL_DUMP_IR=1`); `analysis/isa_diff.py` compares two dumps |

| The store costs more than expected | `gemm/flydsl_gemm_epilogue.md` §2–3 |
| Memory-bound with a linear tile order: tiles that share a panel land on different XCDs | `gemm/flydsl_gemm_schedule_and_locality.md` §2 |
| Stalls on `s_waitcnt` | `gemm/flydsl_gemm_schedule_and_locality.md` §4, `hardware/gfx950/memory_and_sync.md` §1 |
| A fixed cost per tile: time not proportional to K | `gemm/flydsl_gemm_attribution.md` §7, `gemm/flydsl_gemm_grid_pricing.md` §6 |
| Clocks drop under load; slower than the instruction count says | `gemm/flydsl_gemm_attribution.md` §4 |

| A change wins on some shapes and loses on others | `gemm/flydsl_gemm_autotune.md` §1–2; `patterns/shape_divergence.md` |

## Rules that hold everywhere

- **Structure before parameters.** Fusion, pipelining and layout changes beat knob tuning; tune last.
- **Reuse the mechanism, re-derive the number.** Constants in the cited kernels (tile and preload tables,
  wait counts, adoption margins, cache thresholds) were tuned on specific shapes.
- Numbers marked *(field)* are measured values: use them for direction and order of magnitude, not as
  targets. *(field, E1)* points to the line under the page's `## Evidence` that gives the conditions.

## Also in AKLR

- **The aiter these cards describe is the baseline**, ROCm/aiter at `AKLR_BASELINE_AITER`
  (`.github/workflows/ci.yaml`): AKLR does not ship, patch or fall back to it, so its `aiter/` paths are that
  revision's, read as reference code. Price aiter through the op's `<contract>_baseline`
  (`aklr/ops/<op>/baseline.py`), the call bench times. At a Point no kernel serves, the api returns a
  `FallbackReason` and its caller runs its own path. AKLR's plugins route a model to plugin ops only
  (`aklr/plugins/README.md`), so an `aklr/ops` kernel runs in a model only where the engine calls its api.
- **Workflow** (`aklr/ops/README.md` § Workflow): export the Points, fill `kernel.sources`, then
  `python -m aklr export check` and `python -m aklr validate --base origin/main`. The local result does not
  count; CI measures. A `platform_failure` "Kineto recorded no kernels for a single call" is a tracer fault: on a
  busy node, wait a few minutes before you rerun (`pitfalls/profiler_misses_kernels.md`).
- **AKLR does not time below about 4 µs.** Its bench runner forces `GPU_FORCE_QUEUE_PROFILING`, and a profiled
  dispatch costs about that however little it does, so a short kernel and its baseline read about the same. A
  Point whose baseline sits near that floor shows no gain in CI: check `baseline.json` before working on it.

## Folders and adding a page

`CONTRIBUTING.md`: what each folder holds, the page kinds, and how a page gets in.

# Critique: fused native-MXFP4 FlyDSL MoE plan (Direction: replace-the-torch-path-with-a-fused-flyd)

**VERDICT: REVISE**

The route is correct: a fused FlyDSL a4w4 MoE built on aiter's afp4_wfp4 stage kernels. Alternatives were checked properly. A bf16-dequant design loses at M and L (report §4.3). The stepping stones cap out below 0.05× (report §1, §6.5). The prior art `90eaf5c4` is numerically wrong at M ≥ 256 (report §4.3). The choice of `mfma_scale 16x16x128` is causally tied to the scale shuffle at `kernel.py:43-44`. The real gaps are the success gate, an expected gain that is wrong, and missing stop and switch conditions. Each of these would change what gets executed this iteration.

## 1. The success gate assumes the wrong incumbent (this changes the plan)

The plan frames the win as "0.016 → 0.8–1.1". But `run_state.json` says otherwise:
- `best_case_times` equals `baseline_case_times` exactly.
- `analysis_evidence.current_mean_case_speedup` and `mean_case_speedup_at_collection` are both 1.0.

So the incumbent the KEEP gate compares against looks like aiter's times, not the 16–63 ms torch path. If so, a first landing at 0.8–1.0 mean is **not kept**. The same goes for the "torch routing glue" fallback (about 0.4× at S, per the plan's own estimate).

What the plan must add:
- Confirm which time the KEEP gate divides by.
- State that the landing target is mean > 1.0 against `best_case_times`.

The arithmetic: S is 20 of 25 Points. If S lands at about 0.97, the 5 M/L Points must average at least about 1.12 to clear 1.0. The plan has to show where that comes from.

## 2. The claimed M-regime gain from "BM=128 at first landing" is mostly already in the baseline

- Report §4.3 says aiter already runs `t128x128x256` at 3816, under token key 4096. 3112 most likely falls in the same bucket.
- So the plan's line "BM=128 sweeps 1.15 GB against 2.11 GB at BM=64 (3816)" compares against a config the baseline does not run. A straight port at BM=128 is about 1.0× at M, not 1.3–1.6×.
- The only first-landing tile gain is at L. At 32768 aiter runs `t64x128x256_w4`. The configs at 10000 and 13152 are not recorded.
- Before claiming a gain anywhere, Step 0 must record **aiter's chosen config at every M/L Point**.

## 3. aiter's builder limits the "port, then race" knob space

`get_flydsl_stage1_kernels` (`/opt/venv/.../aiter/ops/flydsl/moe_kernels.py:200-214`) sets these limits:
- With fp4 A, `tile_m ∈ {32, 64, 128}`.
- `tile_n ∈ {32, 64, 128}` at tm=32, and `{64, 128}` otherwise.
- Stage 2 also caps at tm=128 (`:299`).

What this means for the plan:
- BM=160, 192 or 256 (Phase B, and the "race 256 later" at L) is **new main-loop code**, not a knob on the port.
- The algorithm specialist's "stage-1 tile_n 256 is legal" is not available from aiter for fp4 A.

The plan should say which Phase B items are knobs of the ported kernel and which are new kernels, and cost them separately. The ported kernel's knobs are `k_wave`, `waves_per_eu`, `b_nt`, `tile_n`, `persist`, and `atomic` vs `reduce`. The cheap way to win at M and L this round is an offline race over these knobs. Where aiter was on an untuned heuristic (report §4.3), this race is the realistic source of the 1.12 M/L average from §1.

## 4. The correctness gate is stricter than the contract and risks burning the iteration

- Step 1 requires the dequantized x to **equal** `kernel._mxfp4(x)`, with integer RNE as the fallback. But the `out` bound is `BaselineRelativeBound` (report §4.4): it scales with aiter's own error, and aiter quantizes with the hardware cvt path.
- Bit-parity with `_mxfp4` is a good diagnostic. It should not block landing.
- **Primary gate:** the `validate` violation fraction (≤ 0.001) on all 25 Points, plus the run-to-run bounded determinism check.
- **Secondary gate:** a bit-exact x/y match.
- Do not switch to the slower integer RNE path unless the primary gate fails. Otherwise the plan can pay a doubled stage-1 epilogue for no scoring reason.

## 5. Missing stop and route-switch conditions

These need to be written down explicitly:
- **Step 0 result: no `has_swiglu_limit` / 1.702 / `+1` epilogue in aiter's stage 1.** Then the epilogue is new code. Budget it, and say whether stage 1 stays bf16-out with a separate y-quant node or gets the fused epilogue.
- **K0 (the custom 128-WG redundant-scan router) is the most novel part.** It is not a port: aiter's sort is the HIP/opus JIT `module_moe_sorting_opus` (report §2), not FlyDSL.
  - Time-box it.
  - If it slips, the documented switch should be a simpler single-pass FlyDSL histogram/scan kernel that is correct but slower. It should not be torch glue, which cannot be kept under §1.
  - Also keep the encoding contract (packed topk slot, `num_valid_ids`, and the sorted, shuffled x-scale layout that `moe_mxfp4_sort` produces) as a written spec checked against aiter's stage-kernel reads. This handoff is where silent bugs live.
- **KEEP and stop criteria after landing:**
  - Mean > 1.0 against `best_case_times`, all 25 Points correct.
  - If the mean is below 1.0 with S below 0.95, stop tuning M/L and inspect the S node count and stream rate first.
  - Get aiter's per-kernel Kineto split at n=256 and 640. The plan defers this to Phase C, but it is cheap and decides how the S margin is spent, so it belongs in Step 0.

## 6. Smaller points

- In `run`, `swiglu_limit` arrives as a scalar keyword. Step 0 item 6 is right; just pass it as a kernel scalar argument, with no `.item()`.
- At 32768, an atomic `out` is 402 MB, below the 32-bit offset limit (`requires_flydsl_stage2_reduce`, `moe_kernels.py:112-116`). The atomic path is valid at every Point.
- The plan rightly keeps `xcd_swizzle=0` until the remap and validity-test order is fixed.
- The plan rightly rejects fixed-order reduce at S.

## What the revised plan should contain

1. A KEEP target that matches the actual incumbent.
2. Step 0 extended with aiter's config at every M/L Point, its per-kernel split at S, and whether the swiglu-limit epilogue exists.
3. A landing built from a faithful port plus a knob race inside aiter's knob space where aiter was untuned.
4. A gate on the validate bound, not on `_mxfp4` bit-parity.
5. A time-boxed K0 with a FlyDSL fallback, not a torch one.
6. BM > 128 and the new main loop deferred, and labelled as new kernels.

directions.rule: Begin every plan (and every lane's plan) with one line naming the direction it pursues: `Direction: <id>` for a direction in this ledger, or `Direction: new | <category> | <title>` for one it does not list. The ledger is ordered by expected_gain_pct, the gain a direction was expected to bring when it was listed; prefer the highest among the OPEN, ACTIVE and KEPT ones. An EXHAUSTED direction has failed repeatedly since its last KEEP and needs new evidence before it is tried again.

ledger.title: Replace the torch path with a fused FlyDSL a4w4 MoE: route/sort, x→MXFP4 quant, stage 1 (gate+up, clamped SwiGLU, MXFP4 requant), stage 2 (down × routing weight), using native scaled fp4 MFMA on the 16x16-preshuffled weights
ledger.expected_gain_reason: Report §5: 26–90× headroom against the candidate. A structurally correct fused kernel takes the score from ~0.016 to ~0.8–1.1. Native fp4 MFMA is needed to match or beat aiter at 3112–32768, where the bf16-dequant practical floor is at or above the baseline.

ledger.title: Stepping stone: replace _unpack's 6-pass dequant chain and the ~20-pass torch _mxfp4 with one vectorized FlyDSL kernel each, keeping the rest of the torch path
ledger.expected_gain_reason: Report §6.5: each piece is a 3–5× gain at most. It does not reach 0.1 speedup but is a quick, low-risk landing if the fused kernel slips.

ledger.title: Per-regime tile-M equal to the sort unit: BM=32 at n≤640, BM=128 at 3112/3816, BM=128–256 at ≥10000
ledger.expected_gain_reason: Neutral on S (aiter is already at BM=32). Large on the 5 M/L Points, where halving weight sweeps against a 2–6.6×-off-roof baseline could give 1.2–2× on each. That is ~5–8% of the mean score.

ledger.title: Compute-leaning main loop for large n: gathered A rows through an XOR-swizzled multi-stage LDS ring prefetched two K-steps ahead, B straight to VGPR, 32x32x64 vs 16x16x128 scaled MFMA, s_setprio around the MFMA block
ledger.expected_gain_reason: L Points have 2.6–3.4× paper headroom (report §5). Even 1.3× on 3–5 Points is ~4–6% of the mean.

ledger.title: XCD-aware tile order plus GROUP_M: keep an expert's row tiles and an M-block's N tiles on one XCD, several row tiles of one expert per column sweep
ledger.expected_gain_reason: Field result: 511→475 µs (−7%) on a fused-MoE stage 1 from the XCD placement. Applies mainly to 5 M/L Points.

ledger.title: Stage-2 combine: race bf16x2 coalesced atomics into out against fixed-order per-route bf16/fp32 rows plus a separate reduce launch, per regime
ledger.expected_gain_reason: Field numbers show a 10–40% swing in stage-2 cost depending on routes per token. Stage 2 is about a third of the call.

ledger.title: Cut graph nodes: fold x quantization and the output zeroing into the sort launch (or the sort into stage 1), preload kernargs, read the expert id before the A loads
ledger.expected_gain_reason: On 20 S Points with ≤1.16–1.24× headroom, saving 1–2 nodes (4–8 µs of 180–190 µs) is 2–4%, which may decide serving at 1.03.

ledger.title: Offline-raced per-shape configuration table (BM, BN, waves, cache policy, atomic vs reduce, MFMA atom) chosen from n_tokens inside the functools.cache compile function
ledger.expected_gain_reason: Tune last. Per-Point picks typically add 2–5% over one config per regime, and it guards against wins on some Points losing on others (a lost workload rejects the candidate).

ledger.title: S-regime grid shape: race tile-N downward (256→128→64) in both stages so 128 experts × (N/BN) blocks fill ≥256 CUs with enough bytes in flight
ledger.expected_gain_reason: The S regime has at most 1.16–1.24× to the hard roof. Grid fill is one of the few levers left on 20 of 25 Points.

ledger.title: Weight-load cache policy per regime and per M-block: non-temporal at n≤640, cached when a sorted neighbour block has the same expert, scale loads always cached
ledger.expected_gain_reason: Field numbers: +1.8% per-block selection, a 6–26% loss if set wrong at multi-block. This is a correctness-free knob with a clear regime flip.

ledger.title: Stage-1 fused epilogue: clamp/SwiGLU in fp32, bf16 round, MXFP4 quantize with shuffled E8M0 in sorted-row order, staged through LDS for 16-byte stores
ledger.expected_gain_reason: The y traffic is small next to the weights, but at L (R=131k routes) store efficiency and the per-lane quant cost become visible.

ledger.title: Persistent or capped grids at large n: launch min(work, k·NUM_CU) workgroups that stride over the device-side tile bound instead of the padded upper-bound grid
ledger.expected_gain_reason: A field gain of 3–5% on the stage it applies to, restricted to the 3–5 large Points.

ledger.title: Skip padding work: send padding rows' A loads out of range (buffer bound returns zero) and skip MFMAs on all-padding sub-tiles
ledger.expected_gain_reason: Small field gains of 1–3% per stage, but cheap and helpful on the near-roof S Points.
